findings.text: Per-CPU chunk offsets are divided into equal sized blocks. The block number comes from division of the offset, the position inside the block comes from masking, and the reverse mapping multiplies and adds. The allocation bitmap address for a block is derived by scaling the block number to words. Masking implies the block size is a power of two, so forward and reverse conversions are inverses.

Freeing an allocation expands to the full surrounding free extent. When the freed range touches the recorded largest free run the extent is taken from that record without searching, otherwise the bitmap is scanned backward and forward to find neighbours. Fully freed edge blocks are recounted, interior blocks fully covered by the range are reset to a canonical empty state, and the chunk empty page tally is adjusted. Chunk level hints are then either fully rebuilt when the free spans blocks or is large, or narrowly updated for a single block interior free.

Each block keeps the earliest free position, the free prefix and suffix lengths that touch the edges, and the largest free run with its start plus a second best run with its start. The earliest position never moves forward, edge lengths change only when the free touches the corresponding edge, a new largest run displaces the old one with the old value usually retained as second best, ties prefer better alignment, and smaller runs can become second best only when located before the largest run.

Chunk aggregate hints have a fast path and a full path. The fast path promotes the second best run to largest and continues scanning after it, while the full path restarts from the earliest free position with no largest run. Both paths then walk every free region described by block metadata and fold each region into the aggregate using the same block update rule.

Address to chunk lookup first tests the dynamic first chunk and then the reserved chunk by range containment that excludes configured head and tail offsets and rejects a missing chunk. Other addresses are shifted into the current processor unit space before page lookup and then mapped from page private storage to the owning chunk. The page lookup backend differs between direct mapping and virtual mapping builds.

Observed chunk state centres on base_addr with nr_pages and head and tail reserves start_offset and end_offset, plus alloc_map, an array md_blocks, an aggregate chunk_md, a count nr_empty_pop_pages, a flag isolated and extensions obj_exts. Observed block state centres on nr_bits with earliest free first_free, edge lengths left_free and right_free, largest run contig_hint with contig_hint_start, and second best scan_hint with scan_hint_start.

Memory cgroup release for per-CPU objects is idempotent and clears the stored charge exactly once. The charged size scales the object size by the possible processor count and adds per object overhead only when kernel memory accounting is enabled, as reported by a global disable flag. Release uncharges through the object stock path and decrements the per-CPU memory state under read side protection before dropping the reference. A separate empty variant performs no work when the feature is disabled.

Allocation tag release subtracts the freed size from the tag associated with the allocation index only when profiling is active and object extensions exist. A separate empty variant exists for builds without the feature, so callers observe either conditional accounting or no effect.
Object cgroup uncharge is a thin entry that forwards the size to a per processor stock refill routine that acquires the stock, applies the refill with uncharge allowed, and releases the stock.

Leak detector lookup holds read side protection across the whole operation and takes the global table lock with interrupts saved only for the table search, then validates the reference before returning. Painting takes the individual object lock with interrupts saved. Callers therefore see table level exclusion for lookup and fine grained exclusion for state change, with safe use after table unlock via the held reference.

Ignoring a per-CPU pointer for leak detection has effect only when the detector is enabled and the pointer is valid. The operation marks the object black which also disables scanning, increments the use count only when non zero, and silently does nothing when no object is found, which covers release paths without a prior allocation record.

Module allocation tag storage moves through reserved, padding, active, unloaded retained and free states in an ordered map. Reservation finds an aligned gap with room for leading padding, records padding separately when alignment shifts the start, and extends the backing store when growth is needed. Release either frees immediately when unused or retains unloaded ranges for reporting until a later sweep reclaims ranges whose counters are all idle. Replacement swaps the owner of an existing range.

All ordered map iteration, gap search, insertion, replacement, erasure and reclamation for module tag storage occur under the map exclusive lock. One reclamation helper assumes the caller already holds that lock, while other helpers acquire and release it internally around the whole map operation.

Allocation profiling defends against incompatible alignment, tag capacity overflow beyond page flag bits, and backing allocation or mapping failure by shutting itself down with a diagnostic and returning an error to the caller. Module counter setup unwinds any counters already allocated for the module before reporting failure, so partial setup is not visible.

Module tag backing starts as a reserved virtual range with an aligned base and grows by appending bulk allocated pages and mapping them, extending shadow coverage and unpoisoning new bytes when needed. Failure during growth releases the newly allocated pages and reports lack of memory. Alternate empty init and free variants exist for configurations without module tag storage. Virtual range allocation prefers the module data range and retries in a fallback range when present.
Object cgroup uncharge and kernel memory disable query are visible across files for per-CPU accounting.
Per-CPU leak ignore and executable memory virtual mapping are visible across files for tagging and module setup.
Block bit length and word length determine bitmap words per block and conversion between offsets and block positions.
Minimum allocation shift and size define indexing granularity for object extensions and overhead scaling.
Page size and shift with module alignment and tag area size govern address range checks and backing growth.

Chunk lookup for other addresses reads the current processor identifier without guarding against migration or hotplug, relying on the property that any processor unit offset yields the same owning chunk.
